content.thinking:
I need to write the whole file carefully in one pass, designing a compact workbench around 1.6m wide, 0.8m deep, 0.9m desk height, using plain objects without requiring extra joints. I'm thinking through whether the builder needs a root joint to organize the parts properly.

I'll keep it simple with a single root joint at the origin and skip extra hinges for drawers or hanging elements, since movement isn't strictly necessary here. For materials, I'm setting up wood grain paints with different axes for legs versus flat surfaces, plus a brass accent color, making sure I stay within the flat-color budget since procedural paints don't count against it. Now I'm laying out the desk geometry itself -- positioning the tabletop, setting its thickness, and centering everything along the depth axis.

Mapping out the full scene now: desk legs at the corners, a drawer cabinet on the right side with three fronts, a lower shelf spanning the left section, and a back riser with posts holding a hanging rod for herb bundles. On the right I'm placing alchemy apparatus -- a brass stand and flask -- while the middle-back holds a stack of books, scales sit slightly left of center, and I'm finishing with a table runner detail.

I also want a stool up front with a green cushion, and I'm figuring out how to generate potion bottles using a lathe operation that revolves a 2D outline around an axis to form a glass body, neck, and cork, with a glowing colored liquid inside.

For herbs, I'm planning to use flat textured cards built from small SVG sprites — lavender and leaf sprigs — mounted on frames so they can hang in bundles, using double-sided cross-shaped cards with slight offsets and rotation for a natural look. I'm sketching the lavender SVG with a green stem and purple ellipse clusters for the flowers.

Beyond herbs, I want gold filigree and rune decals on the drawers and book cover, using transparent-cutout SVG textures mapped onto thin plane geometries so the ornament reads as etched metal. For hardware details like corner brackets and rivets, I'm planning to use small boxes and merged sphere geometries, importing BufferGeometryUtils to combine the rivet studs into a single efficient mesh.

Writing helper functions...

Adding more shape helpers and color definitions...

Now I'm constructing the desk itself: the top slab with trim edges, brass corner caps, and the leg assembly with wider foot pieces for stability.

Adding knee braces and gold brackets at the leg tops, plus the back panel and lower shelf positioned between the legs and cabinet.

Placing the drawer front panel with an inset brass ring torus and gold fleur ornament decal, then starting on the top runner piece spanning the cabinet width.

Working out the cloth drape on the desk: a flat top section sitting at the surface, a hanging front flap dropping over the edge, and a pointed triangular tip extruded at the bottom for a decorative hem.

For the color, I'm making the cloth cream-colored with green vertical stripes by painting based on x-position, checking distance from the stripe centers so the pattern repeats across the surface and carries over onto the hanging flap too.

Next I'm adding a diamond decal onto the flap, tiny brass or cream tassels at the corners, and a draping green cloth panel hanging off the left side with gold trim, before placing items on top of the chest like a mortar and pestle with a white marble bowl and herbs inside.

Then I'm working out a riser structure with two posts, a crossbeam with finials, and a shelf board to hold additional items like a crystal cluster in a brass bowl on the left side.

Checking the overlap, the bundles hang above the bottles with enough vertical clearance. Now I'm adding decorative curved brackets on the sides of the shelf posts, extruding an outline shape and orienting it outward from each post toward the desk.

Then I'm building the book stack — five books of varying width with slight rotation, each composed of a colored cover box and a cream page block inset slightly so the pages peek out along the edges.

I'll widen the pages box to 0.31 so cream edges peek out slightly beyond the cover at both ends, keeping the spine color visible along the depth since the pages sit inset in z, then add gold bands along the spine for detail.

I'm thinking through how to handle rotation: rather than rotating entire book groups (which would complicate aligning child parts), I'll keep books axis-aligned and just shift positions slightly for a jaunty, unrotated stacking effect, writing a book-building helper that computes child offsets locally.

For decals I'm using a facing direction based on yaw along the z-axis. Now I'm placing the scales: a brass pillar around 0.4 units tall with a beam at y=1.3 spanning roughly ±0.17 along x, pans hanging from thin rod chains down to y=1.05, each holding a crystal or herb, and I'm checking that the pan positions near x=-0.12 don't collide with the riser post at x=-0.15.

I'm nudging things to avoid overlap: shifting the riser post, centering the scale near x=0.0 so pans span -0.17 to 0.17 (plus radius), and moving the books over to x≈0.34 so their 0.3-unit width no longer clips the pans or the scale beam area.

Now I'm placing the apparatus on the right side near x=0.68, clear of the desk edge — a brass tripod stand with a candle/lamp base and flame glow, three rods rising to a torus ring at y=1.1, and a round flask sitting at y=1.22.

Still writing flask geometry...

I'll add a small white highlight ellipse and bubble decals to the flask, with a lighter neck top for readability, then replicate that style for the glass bottles with corks. For the condenser, I'm sweeping a thin pale spiral coil path connecting the first flask's neck to a second flask placed at the table edge, routing the pipe upward then across to the second vessel's position.

Now I'm positioning a curved brass support pole near the flask, with a hanging purple bulb attached via a chain or arm extending from the pole's top.

I'm checking for collisions between the bulb and the flask sphere, nudging their x-coordinates slightly apart so they don't overlap, then verifying the adjusted flask position still clears the second flask below it.

Now I'm placing a wooden test-tube rack with five glowing tubes near the front right of the cabinet top, plus a crystal bowl and purple crystal nearby. I'm also sketching out a marble mortar using a lathe profile outline with a sequence of coordinate points defining its curved shape.

For the pestle, I'm positioning it as a tilted capsule resting against the bowl, and adding a clump of green herb-like spheres squashed into the mortar, then starting to scatter loose herb bundles across the desk surface.

Now I'm figuring out how to lay a lavender bundle flat on the table using card frames placed along a line with steep lean angles and a flow direction to simulate it lying stretched out, keeping the placement loose and approximate since exact orientation won't matter much visually. I also note that frames without a bone just default to the root joint, which should work fine here.

For the desk clutter, I'm adding a brass scoop assembled from a lathe-turned bowl and handle rod sitting on a runner, scattering tiny dried petal discs, tucking cream parchment scrolls into a hanging bag on the left side of the desk, and placing a brass lantern with a glowing green core hanging from a bracket near the left front leg.

Now I'm working out the lantern's hanging mechanism more precisely with a bracket rod extending from the desk's top front edge, a chain dropping down, and a small gem pendant below the lantern sphere. For the lower shelf, I'm planning a lathe-turned amphora-style green bottle, a wooden crate holding card-based plants, a squashed sphere grain sack with a tie, and a few small bottles.

I'm placing these items along the shelf with specific x-coordinates, then shifting to design a front stool with splayed square legs, positioning its seat height and yaw rotation relative to the desk.

Adding seat cushion and brass piping...

I'm also adding plank seam lines and nail stud details to the wood surface for texture.

Skipping extra props like a floor rug. For contact, I'm checking that stool legs and feet touch the ground properly around y=0, and estimating the overall model height at roughly 1.7m with the riser posts and apparatus pole as the tallest elements. I'm placing the riser posts with wood material and brass cone caps at the top.

Now I'm working out the crossbeam connecting the posts, then positioning a brass hanging rod with sphere end caps that runs between the posts near the top, adjusting its placement so it threads properly through the post structure.

Next I'm planning three flower bundles spaced along the rod, each with a small gold ribbon tie and lavender cards representing stems and blossoms, oriented so they hang upside down (stems up, blossoms down) as seen from downstream.

Checking proportions so bundle bottoms roughly align with bottle tops near the shelf, then sketching a bottle-generating function that lathes a flask profile with a tapered neck, adds a cork cylinder and a gold wire ring, and attaches a label.

I'm considering a simple highlight for the glass but deciding it's not worth the complexity given the bottle's curved surface -- skipping the inner liquid layer too since it won't be visible through a solid outer shell, and just keeping a single tinted glass lathe for the whole bottle.

Now I'm separating the neck from the body: the body gets the potion's solid glow color while the neck uses a paler glass tone, defining lathe profile points for each section so they connect smoothly at the shoulder. I'm adding a thin pale rim ring at the base using a small torus for a subtle glass-foot detail.

I'm thinking through variants next — a taller bottle by scaling y, and square-ish shapes — parameterized by sx/sy scale factors applied to each lathe part, plus a palette of jewel-tone potion colors (purple, blue, green, amber, pink, teal). For other prop types I'm sketching test tubes as simple cylinders, and crystal clusters built from a hex-prism cylinder topped with a cone, rotated for variation.

For the crystal helper function, I'm building each crystal's geometry by translating the cylinder base and cone tip into position, merging them into one shape, then applying a tilt rotation around the base before placing it at the target coordinates — need to make sure the cylinder and cone geometries share compatible attributes so they can merge cleanly.

Now I'm sketching a gold filigree SVG ornament for the drawer decals, designing a diamond-and-curl shape with gold stroke on a small viewBox, sized so the stroke width stays crisp at the final scale.

Designing more decorative SVG motifs now — a diamond runner pattern, a small star emblem for book spines, a rotated star-flower cushion pattern, and starting on a lavender sprig icon.

Now I'm switching to a white flower variant with pink-white circles and yellow centers, then sketching a lathed brass scale/balance structure—base profile, beam rod with flat caps and small end spheres, and a finial with sphere and cone on top, plus a cross-arm center ornament.

Working out the hanging pans...

I'll suspend three gold rods from each rim point up to a shared apex per pan, then fill the pans with contents -- a blue crystal on one side, green herbs on the other -- plus brass weight cubes. I'm targeting around 350 total parts, writing the pan and rod generation in loops for efficiency, and deciding to skip a woven floor mat for now.

Next I'm placing desk items: a mortar near (-0.52, 0.9, 0.05), a brass candle holder with flame around (-0.74, 0.9, 0.28), and a small crystal bowl nearby, checking radii so they don't overlap, with herb piles toward the front left.

On the right side, I'm positioning a test-tube rack around (0.6, 0.9, 0.1), another crystal bowl near (0.74, 0.9, 0.3), and a lavender bundle lying diagonally in front of the rack near (0.4, 0.9, 0.12), adjusting positions to avoid the rack's footprint overlapping the bundle.

I'm also checking the book stack and apparatus for collisions—the apparatus pole near x=0.46 clips into the book stack's extent, so I'm shifting the books' center to around x=0.3 with a slight yaw, shortening the book arms, and resizing the pan radius to keep everything just clear of the pole.

Checking flask positions for desk overhang and clearances, then working out the tripod stand geometry—legs, ring support, and flask sphere placement with brass rod dimensions.

Now I'm placing the candle and flame under the lamp base, making sure the flame height stays clear of the flask bottom, then moving on to the neck and condenser tube path with its curved pipe coordinates.

Still writing the coil geometry...

Now I'm setting up flask2 with its glowing green sphere and pale neck rod connecting to the pipe, then moving on to build the pole structure with a rod and curved arm at the top.

Next I'm placing a hanging bulb off the pole's arm with a collar and checking its distance stays reasonable from the flask center, then confirming the left riser pole and lantern elements are already handled.

Now I'm starting to write the actual build code, importing Three.js utilities and setting up geometry merging helpers...

Still writing imports... I'm second-guessing whether "three/addons" paths resolve properly in this harness, so rather than risk it I decide to skip merging geometries entirely and just place individual pieces like rivets directly, capping their count around sixty to stay within budget.

Still writing merge helper...

Then I'm setting up the rivet merging approach, translating merged spheres into model space with the part rooted at the origin joint, so I can reuse this for studs and petals. I'm also defining a color type alias and a helper function that wraps part creation with options for rotation, scale, name, texture, and flatness, rooted at the joint I just created.

Adding box, cylinder, and decal plane helpers...

Adding the desk top geometry now, with trim bands along the front, back, and sides to give the edges a proud lip, plus seam lines between planks for detail.

Still writing desk details...

Working out the knee brace angle for the left leg, I'm checking that a -45° z-rotation tilts the brace's top end toward +x so it connects the leg bottom to the apron correctly.

Now I'm laying out the apron boxes (front and back, between the left leg and cabinet edge), the under-shelf back panel, and the lower shelf with its front lip rail, positioning each by width, height, and depth with the appropriate center coordinates.

I'm also constructing the cabinet body itself: the main box, plinth, front frame stiles and rails separating drawer openings, then sketching out drawer face positions and heights across the three drawer rows.

Still placing drawer faces, inset panels, and small ring/torus ornament details on each drawer front...

For the cabinet I'm skipping extra decals on the right side and brass corner caps since they're already covered, and I'm noting the rig just needs a root joint with meta baked in. For the drawer stripe pattern, I'm writing a paint function that uses distance bands from a center point to assign green, gold, or cream colors.

Now I'm placing the runner and flap boxes, adjusting their z-position so the cloth drapes properly over the lip edge, then starting an extruded pointed flap shape with a polygon outline.

For the tassels, I'm planning small cones or spikes at each corner pointing downward, with gold spheres at the tips for decoration.

Now I'm working out the green drape's placement, using mottled green paint for texture, and figuring out where to position a hanging lantern so it doesn't awkwardly overlap the drape or runner — deciding to mount it from a bracket on the left side instead.

Scroll cylinders sticking out of the bag top, visible only from the side. Now I'm sketching a helper function to hang bundles of herbs from a point, scattering card-like billboards around a jittered frame position and orienting them with a lean angle so they droop downward from a pivot at the root bone.

I'm also working out a second function for lying bundles, where cards are laid nearly flat along a flow direction with slight jitter and spin variance to mimic sprigs like lavender fanned out from a tie point.

Now I'm drafting upright mortar herbs and potted crate plants using similar card-frame setups but with different lean angles and radial or cyclic flow functions, then building the crate itself with wood planks, brass corner trim, and a soil box inset at the top.

Shifting to a burlap sack with a squashed sphere body, tied neck, flared frill top, and rope torus details, then starting on a lathed amphora-style bottle shape with a custom body outline.

Adding shape C for a bulb-bellied bottle, then consolidating into a single function parameterized by shape index. I'm making sure the glow helper works generically with the Part type's mesh property, and sketching a small parchment label plane positioned against the curved body at the bottle's widest radius.

Checking the label's edge sag against the curve to make sure it sits flush rather than poking through, and planning a cream parchment-with-seal texture for shapes A and C. Now I'm moving on to building the test tube rack from boxes: a base, two upright end supports, and a top bar.

For the tubes themselves, I'm working out how each one slots through the rack bar with colored liquid, a pale glass top section, and a small cork, making sure the dimensions line up so the bar appears to pass around rather than through the glass. Then I'm starting on the brass candle dish using a lathe profile.

Now I'm shaping the candle itself with its flame and holder, then designing the brass bowl of crystals as another lathe profile, checking the path points don't self-intersect so the geometry stays clean.

I'm writing a helper function to build each crystal from merged cylinder and cone geometries, rotating and tinting them before adding a glow effect so they scatter naturally inside the bowl.

Now I'm setting flat shading so the geometry reads as faceted crystal rather than smooth, making sure the merged non-indexed geometry works with computeVertexNormals for crisp edges. Then I'm laying out the left shelf: positioning the board, bracket, and a row of small bottles at specific heights and x-offsets along the shelf.

Next I'm shaping the left post's scroll bracket as an extruded outline, defining the points that curve from the post down toward the desk surface.

Switching to post-top finials with brass spheres and cones, then thinking through the stack of books—picking colors like blue, crimson, maroon, green, and a small purple volume, each with slightly different heights, and stacking them cumulatively upward from the base.

Now I'm defining a book-building function that places a cover box and a set of pages slightly inset, reasoning about which face of the book should show the visible page edges versus the spine so it reads as a physically plausible standing book.

Adding spine bands and corner caps...

Adding an ornament plane to the top cover, oriented so the drawing reads upright when viewed from above with front at the bottom, then varying yaw angles slightly per book for a natural stacked look. I'm also considering adding a small ribbon bookmark hanging from the front as a box-shaped strip.

Now I'm building a stool: a rotated seat with four angled legs, a square seat plank, apron boxes beneath the seat on each side for support, and connecting rungs between the legs lower down for stability.

Adding cushion with brass trim details...

Building the lantern's brass ring lattice and teal glow core, then a gem pendant below. Skipping extra tassel/sign details, keeping the floor simple, and adding hanging herb bundles (lavender, green, white) on the right side.

Writing SVG code for lavender sprigs with stem and alternating purple bud ellipses...

Still writing SVG elements...

Still writing SVG code...

Now I'm designing a cushion flower icon with eight rotated petals around a center circle, and adding gold trim details like a brass rod and hem along the bottom of the green drape flap.

Adding the crate and plant cards...

Still placing scene objects...

Scattering tiny flattened purple spheres for petals across the runner with randomized seed positions, then checking the overall color budget stays manageable — mostly flat strings plus a few cel-shaded paints for brass, keeping total under roughly 30-60 distinct colors. Now finalizing naming conventions (box, cyl, sph, torus, lathe) before writing out the complete scene code.

I'm building a lathe helper function that generates rotated profile shapes with optional x/y scaling of the outline points, then designing a bottle-building function that uses it to construct labeled potion bottles with configurable shape, scale, and color.

I'm working out torus ring orientations for decorative bands around the bottle — figuring out how to rotate rings into vertical versus horizontal planes depending on which axis I spin them around — and setting up a cone shape for a tassel decoration, flipping its rotation so the apex points downward. I'm also planning a glowing flame effect using a cone with adjustable glow strength.

For the liquid flask, I'm adding a small white highlight plane positioned on the sphere's surface to simulate a specular reflection, calculating a normalized direction vector so the highlight sits naturally on the upper-left front of the glass at a small scale.

Now I'm sketching the curved highlight shape as an SVG path with a thick white stroke, sized to match the flask's proportions, and skipping this treatment for the simpler bottles. Then I need to finish the build function with the final return statement, double-check that typing works for rotation and scale fields using the V3 number arrays, and confirm that all my helper utilities—frame, rng, catmull, spiral, paint, mottle, grain, and INK—are actually being used somewhere, with INK serving as the seam/border color for planks.

Writing stud generation code...
